findings.title: SSE stream hard cap covers only Phase 1 — verdict, self-critique and moderation run unbounded past it
findings.claim: In compare_from_text_streaming, asyncio.wait_for(STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS) wraps ONLY the two _fetch_product_data calls; every await after it (the profile gather, generate_comparison, _apply_self_critique, moderate_output) is unbounded, so the SSE stream can stay open for the hard cap PLUS the OpenAI client's 120s ceiling.
findings.evidence: scs:3577-3583 `product_data = await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.gather(self._fetch_product_data(...), self._fetch_product_data(...)), timeout=STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS)`. An awk sweep of lines 3584-4049 (the rest of the generator) returns exactly 4 awaits, none wrapped: `await _profile_task` (3795), `await generate_comparison(...)`, `await self._apply_self_critique(...)`, `await _safety.moderate_output(...)`. generate_comparison (extraction_service.py:2201) contains no asyncio.wait_for; the only bound is the module-level client at extraction_service.py:49 `timeout=httpx.Timeout(120.0, connect=30.0)`. Contrast the NON-streaming path: scs:2818-2833 wraps the WHOLE _compare_from_text_impl in wait_for(STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS). The module comment at scs:1139-1143 asserts the opposite of what the code does: 'A runaway scraper or slow GPT response cannot extend the SSE stream past this many seconds', and the compare_from_text docstring at 2803-2805 says it gives the sync path 'the same ceiling the streaming path already has'.
findings.failure_scenario: OpenAI is slow/degraded (the repo's own recorded state: OpenAI 429 with retries). A streaming compare finishes Phase 1 at 24s, then generate_comparison hangs. The SSE connection stays open ~30s + up to 120s = ~150s, past the mobile client's 120s axios timeout (CLAUDE.md, api.ts). The user sees the stage checklist stall after 'Generating verdict...' and the request dies client-side with no `error` event, while the server keeps a connection + an in-flight GPT-4o call alive. The published 25/30s SSE budget is simply not enforced.
findings.fix_sketch: Move the wait_for to wrap the whole generator body the way compare_from_text does (or add a second wait_for around the post-Phase-1 tail with the residual budget: `remaining = STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS - elapsed`), and on timeout yield the existing best-available PARTIAL. Cheapest correct version: compute a deadline at entry and pass `timeout=max(0.5, deadline - time.monotonic())` to a wait_for around generate_comparison + critique + moderation.
findings.verify_evidence: Re-derived. scs:3576-3583 is the ONLY asyncio.wait_for inside compare_from_text_streaming (def spans 3396-4055; an awk sweep of that range returns exactly one wait_for hit, at 3577) and it wraps only the two _fetch_product_data calls. I independently listed every await after 3583: 3590/3649 (inside the two except handlers), 3795 'behavior_profile, demographics_profile = await _profile_task', 3829 'comparison, usage = await generate_comparison(...)', 3842 'await self._apply_self_critique(', 4015 'await _safety.moderate_output(_l3_text)', 4046 (cancel) -- none wrapped. generate_comparison is extraction_service.py:2201; an awk sweep of 2201-2600 returns ZERO wait_for/timeout= hits, so its only bound is the module client at extraction_service.py:49 'timeout=httpx.Timeout(120.0, connect=30.0)' (AsyncOpenAI, default max_retries). Contrast verified: scs:2818-2833 wraps the WHOLE _compare_from_text_impl. Two doc contradictions confirmed verbatim: scs:1139-1143 'asyncio.wait_for(...) wraps the data-fetch + scoring + verdict pipeline' and CLAUDE.md:324 'outermost asyncio.wait_for on streaming + non-streaming compare_from_text'. Both are false for the streaming path. Scenario nit (does not change the verdict): SmartCompareApp/src/services/api.ts:20 'timeout: 120000' is the AXIOS default; the SSE path is a fetch/ReadableStream reader, so the client symptom is a stalled reader rather than an axios timeout.

findings.title: _get_price has no try/finally — up to 4 speculative Serper searches plus N adapter fetches orphan on every race timeout
findings.claim: _get_price (5044-6976, 1,932 lines) creates speculative asyncio.ensure_future tasks for discovery search_web and the direct adapters, but contains ZERO try/finally, so when the outer asyncio.wait_for(_PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT=15s) or the stream hard cap cancels it, _cancel_prefetched_discovery()/_cancel_prefetched_direct() are never reached and those tasks run to completion with their results discarded.
findings.evidence: AST walk of _get_price: `try/finally at []` (no finally block anywhere in the function). Speculative task kickoff at scs:5354/5357/5360/5362 (`_prefetched_discovery.append((..., asyncio.ensure_future(search_web(...))))` — up to 4 PAID Serper calls) and scs:5455/5466/5505/5515/5534 (`_prefetched_direct[...] = asyncio.ensure_future(asyncio.gather(...))` for shopify / algolia / sitemap / jsonapi / the 6 BH-GCC adapters). The only cleanup is the plain-statement calls at 5788, 5939, 6077, 6171 and 6582 — all reachable only on the normal-flow short-circuit paths. Immediately after kickoff the function performs an UNBOUNDED await at scs:5841 `search_results = await search_product_prices(search_query, region_info['code'])` (the default flag-OFF branch; serper's own httpx ceiling is 15.0s, serper_service.py:_serper_timeout), i.e. the most likely place for the 15s race cancel to land. The comment at 5364-5368 states these cancels exist 'so no orphan Serper calls survive' — the guarantee holds only on the paths that reach them.
findings.failure_scenario: A cold compare on a _pf_eligible category (fragrances/fashion/etc.): the 4 discovery search_web tasks and the adapter gathers are kicked off, then Serper Shopping takes >15s (the documented cold-query condition — CLAUDE.md's eval note says COLD smoke20 hits the cap by design). wait_for cancels _get_price at line 5841; the 4 ensure_future tasks are NOT cancelled (they are independent Tasks) and complete in the background, burning Serper credits and executor threads for results nobody reads. Two products per compare doubles it. Same leak fires on the STREAM_HARD_CAP cancel and on any un-handled raise inside the function.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap the body from the first ensure_future onward in `try: ... finally: _cancel_prefetched_discovery()` (which already chains _cancel_prefetched_direct). That one finally makes every cancel/raise path converge on the existing cleanup with no behaviour change on the happy path (the cancels are idempotent — they check `.done()` and clear the containers).
findings.verify_evidence: Structure CONFIRMED, headline cost REFUTED, so P1 -> P2. AST walk of _get_price (AsyncFunctionDef 5044-6976): 18 Try nodes, and the list of tries with a finalbody is EMPTY -- zero finally blocks, as claimed. Speculative kickoff verified at 5353/5356/5359/5361 (up to 4 asyncio.ensure_future(search_web(...))) and 5455/5466/5505/5515/5534; the outer cancel verified at 4261-4264 'asyncio.ensure_future(asyncio.wait_for(_timed_task("price", self._get_price(...)), timeout=_PHASE1_TIMEOUTS["price"]))' with _PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT=15.0 (scs:1150). The unbounded await is at 5842 (finding said 5841, off by one): 'search_results = await search_product_prices(search_query, region_info["code"])' in the else branch. Ran a zero-network asyncio model: an ensure_future task created inside a coroutine that an outer wait_for cancels DOES run to completion ('orphan serper COMPLETED (nobody read it)') -- so the leak is real. WHY DOWNGRADED: the claim 'burning Serper credits' does not hold. ensure_future dispatches the HTTP request within milliseconds; Serper bills on request receipt, so a cancel 15s later saves zero credits. The cleanup calls at 5788/5939/6077/6171/6582 save credits only on the EARLY short-circuit paths, which already run today. The real residual is background tasks / httpx connections / to_thread executor slots outliving the request that spawned them (~18 per timed-out compare) -- measurable bloat, not a P1 spend defect.

findings.title: 128 synchronous Supabase .execute() calls run on the asyncio event loop inside async def, on a single-worker uvicorn
findings.claim: Every DB helper is `async def` but uses the SYNC supabase-py client, so each .execute() is a blocking HTTP round trip on the one event loop; an AST count finds 128 such calls inside async defs across app/services + app/api, with exactly one counter-example that does it correctly.
findings.evidence: database_service.py:12 `from supabase import create_client, Client` (supabase==2.31.0 sync client, requirements.txt:156) and e.g. :91 `response = client.table('users').select('*').eq('id', user_id).single().execute()` inside `async def get_user_by_id`. AST count of `.execute()` inside async def: referral_service 33, admin_routes 21, database_service 19, auth_service 11, product_data_service 6, analytics_service 5, structured_comparison_service 5, auth_routes 5, reengagement_service 4, home_routes 4, profile_routes 4, feedback_service 3, usage_service 3, push_service 2, audit_service 1, drug_database_service 1, verdict_critique_service 1 = 128. The single correct pattern is spec_spine_service.py:310 `row = await asyncio.to_thread(_lookup_supabase_sync, key, table)`. Deployment is one worker: Procfile / railway.json `uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT` with no --workers. docs/CONTEXT_DECISIONS_BUGS.md:83 records the architecture claim 'AsyncIO throughout | Non-blocking, handles concurrent requests', which the code does not implement.
findings.failure_scenario: Two users compare simultaneously. User A's request hits `await _profile_task` -> _fetch_behavior_profile -> a blocking Supabase select. For the full Supabase RTT the event loop cannot advance ANY other coroutine — user B's SSE stream, the price race's asyncio timers, and the wait_for deadlines all stall. Because the deadline arithmetic (15s price race, 25/30s hard cap) is wall-clock, a burst of concurrent Supabase round-trips directly converts into hard-cap timeouts for unrelated requests. This is also why the free-unit test suite hangs (docs/investigations/2026-08-24-audit-implementation-handoff.md §2).
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap each helper's terminal call in `await asyncio.to_thread(lambda: <builder>.execute())` (the spec_spine_service pattern), starting with the request-path hot set: database_service.get_user_by_id / get_user_comparisons / save_comparison, usage_service, auth_service token verify. Longer term switch to `create_async_client`. Cap the default executor explicitly so scraper to_thread work cannot starve DB offload.
findings.verify_evidence: Independently re-derived with my own AST sweep over app/services + app/api + app/utils counting .execute() calls inside AsyncFunctionDef bodies: total 128, and the per-file distribution matches the finding EXACTLY (referral_service 33, admin_routes 21, database_service 19, auth_service 11, product_data_service 6, analytics_service 5, structured_comparison_service 5, auth_routes 5, reengagement_service 4, home_routes 4, profile_routes 4, feedback_service 3, usage_service 3, push_service 2, audit_service 1, drug_database_service 1, verdict_critique_service 1). database_service.py:12 'from supabase import create_client, Client' with requirements.txt:156 'supabase==2.31.0' (sync) and :91 'response = client.table("users").select("*").eq("id", user_id).single().execute()' inside 'async def get_user_by_id'; grep confirms ZERO to_thread in database_service / usage_service / auth_service / referral_service / audit_service. Single worker confirmed: Procfile and railway.json both 'uvicorn app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port $PORT', no --workers. KNOWN-ITEM STATUS CLAIM VERIFIED CORRECT: docs/CONTEXT_DECISIONS_BUGS.md:83 still asserts '| AsyncIO throughout | Non-blocking, handles concurrent requests |'. ONE EVIDENCE ERROR (does not change the verdict): the free-unit test hang is documented at CLAUDE.md:440 and docs/investigations/2026-08-24-audit-implementation-handoff.md:59-63 as LIVE curl_cffi calls to retailer sites in executor threads (issue #70), NOT as blocking Supabase -- that citation is a misattribution.

findings.title: 124 blocking Redis/budget calls inside 52 async defs; the ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD escape hatch covers 4 read sites and is default OFF
findings.claim: cache_service.redis_client is a blocking client (Upstash REST over httpx.Client) and all of cache_service's and api_budget_service's helpers are sync; an AST sweep finds 124 unawaited calls to them inside async def bodies, while the documented mitigation only routes 4 of them.
findings.evidence: cache_service.py:18-44 builds a SYNC client; :540-548 states plainly 'The module-level `redis_client` is a BLOCKING (httpx.Client) client, so every get_cached from an async orchestrator method stalls the single worker loop for the full Upstash RTT (~6-8 guaranteed per warm compare, ~12-20 cold)'. serper_service.py:207-210 measures one such round trip at 163ms. The offload dispatch is scs:838-851 `_cache_get_async`, and grep shows exactly four call sites: scs:4317, 4318, 4835, 5084 — all READS. Every write (set_cached at scs:4738, 4845, 4891, 5135, 5224, 6650, 6681, 6736, 6945, 5799; review_service 664/695/715/729/834/913; sitemap 648/678; price_service 14051) and every api_budget call (has_budget / record_usage / record_failure / record_success / is_circuit_closed / try_consume_* at scs:1374/1399/1402/1410/1448/1478/1481/1489, serper_service 537/664/876/968/1004/1045, algolia 316/319/361/365/371/757/787, noon 174/411/414/485/504/507, unbxd 202/205/211/232, youtube 99/125/175/184/187/207/230, image_service 249, rating_service 296, review_service 784/878) is inline. Direct redis_client use inside async def: auth_service 549/551/567/569/580, usage_service 224/226/228/230, model_router_service 107. The flag itself defaults OFF (cache_service.py:549 `os.getenv('ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD', '')`).
findings.failure_scenario: One warm streaming compare performs on the order of 20-30 of these blocking round trips (4 cache reads + ~10 cache writes + ~6-12 budget/breaker reads and writes). At the module's own 163ms measurement that is 3-5 seconds of event-loop stall per compare, charged to EVERY concurrent request, inside a 15s price race and a 25/30s hard cap. Under two concurrent compares the second one's Phase-1 timers expire on stall alone.
findings.fix_sketch: Promote the _cache_get_async dispatch into a pair of async wrappers (`cache_get_async` / `cache_set_async`) that use asyncio.to_thread, then mechanically convert the 124 enumerated sites; batch the api_budget breaker+budget read into ONE memoised async check per provider per request (the pattern serper_service._serper_budget_ok already uses). Flip ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD to default ON once the write path is covered.
findings.verify_evidence: Re-derived. cache_service.py:18-44 builds a SYNC client (upstash_redis.Redis over httpx, or redis.from_url); the module's own docstring at :539-548 states the hazard verbatim ('The module-level redis_client is a BLOCKING (httpx.Client) client, so every get_cached from an async orchestrator method stalls the single worker loop for the full Upstash RTT (~6-8 guaranteed per warm compare, ~12-20 cold)') and :549 reads os.getenv('ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD', '') -- default OFF confirmed. Independent grep for _cache_get_async: definition at scs:838 plus EXACTLY four call sites -- 4317, 4318, 4835, 5084 -- all reads. The absence claim holds. The 163ms figure is quoted in-tree at serper_service.py:207-210. Spot-checked the cited inline sites: scs:4738/4845/5135 are bare set_cached(...), scs:1374/1448 are bare 'is_circuit_closed(...) and has_budget(...)'. COUNT NIT: my own AST sweep (unawaited calls to get/set/delete_cached, has_budget, record_usage/failure/success, is_circuit_closed, serper_gate_allows, the _redis_* helpers, plus any redis_client.* attribute call, inside async defs) totals 111, not 124 -- the exact number depends on which helpers are counted. Substance and severity unchanged.

findings.title: Circuit breaker half-open state admits unlimited calls — half_open_calls is written to 0, read, and never incremented anywhere
findings.claim: CB_HALF_OPEN_MAX_CALLS = 1 is never enforced: `half_open_calls` is set to 0 on the OPEN->HALF_OPEN transition and compared at the gate, but no code path in the repository ever increments it, so after the 10-minute cooldown every caller is admitted instead of one probe.
findings.evidence: Repo-wide grep for `half_open` in *.py (excluding the non-deployed backend/ copy) returns exactly five hits: api_budget_service.py:267 (the constant), :505 `state['half_open_calls'] = 0`, :511 `return state.get('half_open_calls', 0) < CB_HALF_OPEN_MAX_CALLS`, and tests/test_api_budget_service.py:277/283/290. record_success (:542-556) sets state back to CLOSED and record_failure (:518-539) increments failure_count — neither touches half_open_calls. The tests do not catch it because test_half_open_blocks_excess_calls (tests/test_api_budget_service.py:281-286) hand-seeds `half_open_calls: 1`, a state production can never write.
findings.failure_scenario: Firecrawl is down; three failures trip the breaker at 10:00. At 10:10 the next compare's Tier-1.5 fan-out dispatches ~6-10 render candidates concurrently; is_circuit_closed returns True for all of them because half_open_calls stays 0, so all of them are attempted (Scrape.do bills ~5 credits each) before any failure result comes back to re-trip the breaker. The designed behaviour is one probe. Repeats every 10 minutes for the whole outage, against a Scrape.do budget of 900/month.
findings.fix_sketch: In is_circuit_closed's HALF_OPEN branch, increment and persist before returning True: `state['half_open_calls'] = state.get('half_open_calls', 0) + 1; _redis_set(_circuit_key(provider), json.dumps(state), ex=_CB_TTL); return state['half_open_calls'] <= CB_HALF_OPEN_MAX_CALLS`. Then replace the hand-seeded test with one that drives the real transition and asserts the second call is refused.
findings.verify_evidence: REPRODUCED with a zero-network run against this tree. Independent grep for half_open over app/ tests/ scripts/ returns exactly 3 hits in app/ (api_budget_service.py:267 constant, :505 state['half_open_calls'] = 0, :511 return state.get('half_open_calls', 0) < CB_HALF_OPEN_MAX_CALLS) -- nothing increments it; record_failure (:518-539) touches only failure_count, record_success (:542-556) only resets state. Repro: stubbed _redis_get/_redis_set with an in-memory dict, drove 3 record_failure('firecrawl') -> state 'open', is_circuit_closed False; rewound tripped_at past CB_RECOVERY_TIMEOUT, then called is_circuit_closed 6 times -> [True, True, True, True, True, True], with half_open_calls still 0 in the persisted state, against CB_HALF_OPEN_MAX_CALLS = 1. The hand-seeded test at tests/test_api_budget_service.py:283 ('half_open_calls': 1) confirms production can never write that value. Severity held at P2 (not higher) because the first failure result re-trips the breaker, so over-admission is bounded to one burst per 10-minute window.

findings.title: Serper — the highest-volume paid provider — has metering but no circuit breaker: record_failure('serper') and is_circuit_closed('serper') have zero call sites
findings.claim: Every other provider guards its calls with is_circuit_closed()/record_failure(); Serper only calls record_usage() on success, and its one gate (serper_gate_allows) is documented as INERT unless SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT is declared — which CLAUDE.md says is unset by default — so a dead Serper endpoint is retried at full rate on every request forever.
findings.evidence: Repo grep of record_failure(/record_success(/is_circuit_closed( shows firecrawl (scs:1374/1402/1410), scrapedo (scs:1448/1481/1489), brightdata (brightdata_service.py:75/89/91), algolia (algolia_service.py:757/787/…), noon (noon_service.py:485/504/507), unbxd (unbxd_service.py:232/202/211), youtube (youtube_service.py:175/207/230) — and for serper only `record_usage('serper')` at serper_service.py:537, 664, 876, 968, 1004, 1045 plus rating_service.py:296. No is_circuit_closed('serper'), no record_failure('serper') anywhere. The only read-side control is serper_gate_allows (api_budget_service.py:234-249), and _serper_gate_engaged (:172-197) returns False unless SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT is set to a positive value; CLAUDE.md states it is 'UNSET by default, and unset means the spend gate is INERT'.
findings.failure_scenario: Serper returns 403 on every /search — the state CLAUDE.md records as live today. Each compare still dispatches all six Serper entry points (unified search, price shopping, price organic, images, and the 4-way discovery fan-out) at their full 15s httpx timeout, per product, on every request, forever. No cooldown ever engages, so the price race spends most of its 15s budget on calls that are known-dead, and the 25/30s hard cap fires on requests that could have degraded instantly. Firecrawl in the identical situation goes quiet for 10 minutes after 3 failures.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `serper` to the guarded set: gate _serper_post's dispatch on is_circuit_closed('serper'), call record_failure('serper') on httpx.TimeoutException and on 5xx/403 responses, record_success('serper') on a 200. Reuse the existing 60s memo (_serper_budget_ok) so the breaker read does not add a blocking round trip per entry point.
findings.verify_evidence: Absence claim independently verified. Repo-wide grep of app/: is_circuit_closed( has 7 call sites (algolia 757, brightdata 75, noon 485, scs 1374 firecrawl, scs 1448 scrapedo, unbxd 232, youtube 175) and record_failure( has 13 (algolia, brightdata, noon, scs firecrawl/scrapedo, unbxd, youtube) -- NEITHER mentions serper. serper's only budget interaction is record_usage('serper') at serper_service.py:537/664/876/968/1004/1045 plus rating_service.py:296, and the read side is _serper_budget_ok -> serper_gate_allows (api_budget_service.py:234-249), inert unless SERPER_LIFETIME_LIMIT>0 per _serper_gate_engaged (:171-197); CLAUDE.md:326 confirms 'UNSET by default, and unset means the spend gate is INERT'. STRONGER THAN THE FINDING CLAIMED: CLAUDE.md:158 documents api_budget_service.py as 'Credit tracking + circuit breakers (Firecrawl/Scrape.do/Serper)' -- a documented status that is FALSE for Serper, which is exactly the reportable case. Note the inert SPEND gate is a deliberate, documented decision (_serper_gate_engaged docstring); the missing FAILURE breaker is addressed nowhere and is the real gap.

findings.title: The one plain asyncio.create_task fire-and-forget left in app/ — the exact pattern the repo's audit convention bans
findings.claim: review_service schedules the L2 DB review persist with a bare asyncio.create_task, so any exception inside save_reviews is swallowed with no log, no Sentry event and no done-callback — the failure mode CLAUDE.md's 'Audit conventions (2026-05-22)' section and app/utils/async_utils.py were written to eliminate.
findings.evidence: review_service.py:697 `asyncio.create_task(save_reviews(cache_key, brand, name, variant, reviews))`. A repo-wide grep for create_task|ensure_future outside structured_comparison_service.py, price_service.py:15550 (managed fan-out tasks) and async_utils.py returns only this line plus three docstring mentions. CLAUDE.md: '`_fire_and_forget(coro, label)` … use for new fire-and-forget tasks; adds done-callback that logs WARNING on exception. Plain `asyncio.create_task()` swallows exceptions and drops audit/personalization writes.' app/utils/async_utils.py:8-14 records that Bundle D 2.B.6 converted 22 such sites in app/api/*.py; this one was missed.
findings.failure_scenario: product_data_service.save_reviews raises (RLS denial, schema drift, Supabase 5xx). The reviews L2 DB cache silently stops being written; every subsequent request for the same product misses L2, re-pays for a Serper search plus a GPT extract, and the 14-day review TTL never materialises. Nothing in logs or Sentry indicates why, because the task's exception is only retrievable from the Task object nobody holds.
findings.fix_sketch: `from app.utils.async_utils import fire_and_forget` then `fire_and_forget(save_reviews(cache_key, brand, name, variant, reviews), label='save_reviews.l2')`. One-line change, matches the 22 already-converted sites.
findings.verify_evidence: Absence claim independently verified. My own grep for 'asyncio.create_task|asyncio.ensure_future' across app/, excluding structured_comparison_service.py and price_service.py, returns exactly one executable line: review_service.py:697 'asyncio.create_task(save_reviews(cache_key, brand, name, variant, reviews))'. The other four hits are docstrings/comments (audit_service.py:20, serper_service.py:211, usage_service.py:216, async_utils.py:10/13). The convention it violates is in-tree twice: CLAUDE.md:283 ('Plain asyncio.create_task() swallows exceptions and drops audit/personalization writes') and app/utils/async_utils.py:8-14 (Bundle D 2.B.6 converted 22 sites in app/api/*.py). Context supporting the failure scenario: the write sits at the exact point the surrounding comment calls load-bearing -- 'persist the COMPLETED extraction BEFORE the optional consult ... otherwise the finished extract_reviews result is lost'.

findings.title: Four adapters' inner curl timeout exceeds the outer _ADAPTER_TIMEOUT, violating the repo's own documented ceiling rule
findings.claim: The prefetched adapters are wrapped in _timeout_none(..., _ADAPTER_TIMEOUT=10.0), but salla, occ, magento_gql and rest_json each pass a 12s timeout to their inner curl_cffi call, so on the 10s cancel the executor thread keeps running for up to 2 more seconds — the exact leak price_service.py:15096-15100 documents as forbidden.
findings.evidence: scs:208 `_ADAPTER_TIMEOUT = 10.0`; scs:5515/5534 wrap every adapter coro in `_timeout_none(lambda …, _ADAPTER_TIMEOUT)`; the adapter set is scs:5422-5445 (woo, salla, occ, magento_gql, unbxd, rest_json, noon, shopify_gcc). Inner ceilings: salla_service.py:58 `_HTTP_TIMEOUT = 12`, occ_service.py:76 `_TIMEOUT = 12`, magento_graphql_service.py:105 `_HTTP_TIMEOUT = 12.0`, rest_json_service.py:53 `_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 12`, woocommerce_service.py:64 `_WOO_TIMEOUT = 10` (exactly at the bound). All are dispatched via asyncio.to_thread (salla 93/207, occ 282, magento 440/484/518/647, rest_json 261/319/404). The rule they violate is stated verbatim at price_service.py:15096-15100: 'a wait_for cannot hard-cancel the run_in_executor thread — so the inner curl timeout MUST be <= the outer bound or the executor thread leaks past the cancel'. Adjacent: shopify_pdp_service.py:103 HTTP_TIMEOUT = 12 inside a loop of up to MAX_REDIRECTS+1 = 4 hops (shopify_pdp_service.py:298-304), i.e. a 48s worst case behind a 10s cancel (flag ENABLE_SHOPIFY_PDP_JSON default OFF).
findings.failure_scenario: ENABLE_BH_GCC_CATALOG_SOURCES is ON in prod (CLAUDE.md), so the catalog rows make several of these adapters fire per compare. A slow storefront hangs; _timeout_none returns None at 10s and the price race moves on, but the thread stays parked in curl.perform() for 2 more seconds. All of these share Python's DEFAULT ThreadPoolExecutor with the Redis offload and every other to_thread scrape (33 sites, no custom executor anywhere), so leaked threads directly reduce the pool available to the next request's scrapes.
findings.fix_sketch: Set each adapter's inner ceiling strictly below _ADAPTER_TIMEOUT (e.g. 8) or derive it from a shared constant, and add a unit test asserting `inner <= _ADAPTER_TIMEOUT - 1` for every module in the _new_adapter_specs list. Separately, install an explicitly sized executor at startup (`loop.set_default_executor(ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=N))`) so the pool size is a decision, not a default.
findings.verify_evidence: Constants re-read in this tree: scs:208 '_ADAPTER_TIMEOUT = 10.0'; salla_service.py:58 '_HTTP_TIMEOUT = 12', occ_service.py:76 '_TIMEOUT = 12', magento_graphql_service.py:105 '_HTTP_TIMEOUT = 12.0', rest_json_service.py:53 '_REQUEST_TIMEOUT = 12', woocommerce_service.py:64 '_WOO_TIMEOUT = 10' (exactly at the bound). All four over-ceiling adapters appear in _new_adapter_specs (scs:5422-5445) and every entry is wrapped '_timeout_none(lambda ..., _ADAPTER_TIMEOUT)' at scs:5543; salla dispatches via 'await asyncio.to_thread(... timeout=_HTTP_TIMEOUT)' at salla_service.py:93/207. The rule is stated verbatim at price_service.py:15095-15100 ('a wait_for cannot hard-cancel the run_in_executor thread -- so the inner curl timeout MUST be <= the outer bound or the executor thread leaks past the cancel'). Reachability checked rather than assumed: CLAUDE.md:328 has ENABLE_BH_GCC_CATALOG_SOURCES 'ON in prod since 2026-06-26', and data/bh_gcc_sources.json carries salla_api 19, magento_graphql 8, rest_json 3, occ_rest 2 rows -- so the mismatch is live, not inert. ONE EVIDENCE ERROR: the 'adjacent' shopify_pdp_service.py claim is wrong -- the module states at :76 that fetch_shopify_pdp_json 'still has no call site', and the only reachable entry (fetch_ucp_json_price via price_service._try_ucp_json_price:13813/13841) runs inside the price cascade, NOT under _ADAPTER_TIMEOUT. Related to the documented #70 class (executor threads a wait_for cannot kill), but these four concrete constants are recorded nowhere in-tree.

findings.title: SSE client-disconnect return skips ALL post-stream side effects — quota metering, history save and analytics
findings.claim: event_generator returns immediately when request.is_disconnected() is true, which is placed BEFORE the post-loop block, so a fully-computed comparison is never metered against the user's free tier (record_comparison), never saved to history (save_comparison_and_track_cohort) and never logged (log_search).
findings.evidence: text_routes.py:493-495 `if await request.is_disconnected(): logger.info(...); return` sits inside the `async for` at :481-492; the analytics/persistence block runs only after that loop falls through, at :508-549 (`fire_and_forget(log_search(...))`, `fire_and_forget(save_comparison_and_track_cohort(...))`, `fire_and_forget(record_comparison(user_id, ...))`). There is no try/finally, so the early return bypasses all three. The counterpart POST route fires the same three at :219-239 unconditionally after the awaited result.
findings.failure_scenario: A free-tier user runs a streaming compare and backgrounds the app (or the mobile client drops the socket) after the last event is generated. The backend already spent the OpenAI + Serper budget for that comparison, but `record_comparison` never runs, so the daily/monthly/lifetime counters do not move and the comparison does not appear in history. Repeating the pattern is an unmetered free-tier bypass that costs real money per repetition, and it silently under-counts the KPI numbers CLAUDE.md says log_search feeds.
findings.fix_sketch: Hoist the post-stream block into a `finally:` around the `async for`, keyed on whether `complete_response` was captured, so a disconnect after the payload was produced still meters and persists. Keep the early `return` for the streaming loop itself.
findings.verify_evidence: Defect confirmed, stated MECHANISM corrected. Verified text_routes.py:481-495: 'if await request.is_disconnected(): logger.info(...); return' sits inside the async for, and the analytics/persistence block (fire_and_forget log_search / save_comparison_and_track_cohort / record_comparison) is at :508-549 after the loop, with no try/finally. CORRECTION: the finding's scenario ('backgrounds the app after the last event is generated') does NOT hold. I enumerated every yield in the generator (3396-4055): ('complete', X) is ALWAYS the final yield on every path (3613, 3636, 3659, 4031, 4040, each followed by a return or end of body), and the disconnect check runs BEFORE the 'complete_response = data' assignment -- so on any disconnect complete_response is None and the guarded 'if complete_response and not had_error' block would be a no-op even with the return removed. Removing the return alone changes only the 'elif had_error' failure log. WHAT SURVIVES, and it is the stronger bug: the 'verdict' event at scs:3898 already carries the ENTIRE payload ('comparison': comparison, winner, value_context, best_for, personalized_insights). A client that reads through 'verdict' and drops the socket receives the full comparison while record_comparison, save_comparison_and_track_cohort and log_search never run -- a repeatable, unmetered free-tier bypass after the OpenAI + Serper spend has already been incurred. P2 held.

findings.title: SSE event_generator has no exception guard around the orchestrator iteration
findings.claim: `async for event_type, data in service.compare_from_text_streaming(...)` is unguarded, so any exception the orchestrator raises after the response has started propagates out of the StreamingResponse body: the client gets a truncated stream with no terminal `error` event, and the failure-path log_search at :542 never fires.
findings.evidence: text_routes.py:477-506 — the generator body has exactly one `if event_type == 'error': had_error = True` branch (:503-504) and no try/except/finally. Because StreamingResponse has already emitted 200 + headers by then, FastAPI's ErrorHandlerMiddleware cannot convert the raise into the unified `{success:false, error, code, request_id}` envelope described in CLAUDE.md; the connection simply ends mid-body.
findings.failure_scenario: compare_from_text_streaming raises anywhere outside its own guarded blocks (e.g. the response_builder assembly, or a TypeError on a malformed scoring payload). The mobile client's fetch+ReadableStream reader sees the stream close after the `scores` event, with no `error` event to branch on, so it renders a half-populated results screen; server-side the only trace is an unstructured traceback with no query context and no `log_search(success=False)` row.
findings.verify_evidence: The premise misreads the flow. The route's async for at text_routes.py:481 is indeed unguarded, but the ORCHESTRATOR guards itself: compare_from_text_streaming opens 'try:' at scs:3475 and closes with 'except Exception as e:' at scs:4042-4050, which logs with exc_info and yields ('error', {...}) as a terminal event. Every await the finding names as a risk -- the response_builder assembly, scoring, generate_comparison, moderation -- is inside that try, so the stated failure scenario (raise -> stream closes mid-body with no error event, no log_search(success=False)) cannot occur: had_error is set at text_routes:503 and the failure log at :542 does fire. Residual gap, and it is small: lines 3396-3474 run BEFORE the try (get_content_safety_service(), _safety.check_query_intent(query), hashlib), as does the except handler's own 'await _cancel_profile_task' at 4046; a raise there, or an asyncio.CancelledError (BaseException, not caught by except Exception), would escape unconverted. That residual is a P3 hardening note, not the P2 defect described.

findings.title: All three Redis-backed auth security controls fail open with zero observability, and logout reports success after a failed revocation
findings.claim: check_account_locked, _is_token_revoked and track_failed_login swallow every exception and return the permissive answer with no log line at all, and logout() returns 'Logged out successfully' even when _revoke_token could not write the blacklist entry — so a Redis outage silently disables brute-force lockout and token revocation with nothing in logs or Sentry to say it happened.
findings.evidence: auth_service.py:554-555 `except Exception: return {'locked': False, 'retry_after': 0}` (no logger call); :571-572 `except Exception: return {'locked': False, 'attempts': 0}`; :581-582 `except Exception: pass`; :313-314 `except Exception: return False  # Fail-open` in _is_token_revoked. _revoke_token (:294-302) does log a warning, but logout (:283-291) returns `{'success': True, 'message': 'Logged out successfully'}` regardless. For contrast cache_service's own helpers all log (`logger.error(f'Redis GET error: {e}')`, cache_service.py:63). CLAUDE.md documents both as active controls: 'Logout revokes via Redis blacklist `revoked:{sha256(token)}` 1h TTL. `verify_token()` checks blacklist before Supabase.' Secondary defect in the same block: at :567-569 the INCR is issued first and `redis_client.expire(key, LOCKOUT_WINDOW_SECONDS)` second — if expire raises after incr succeeded, the except swallows it and the counter key is left with NO TTL, so once it reaches 5 the account is locked permanently and check_account_locked returns `retry_after: max(ttl, 0)` = 0 because ttl is -1.
findings.failure_scenario: Upstash has an incident. Every check_account_locked returns locked:false and every _is_token_revoked returns False, so (a) an attacker gets unlimited password guesses against a known email for the duration, and (b) tokens revoked at logout are accepted again for their full lifetime. Operators see nothing: no WARNING, no Sentry breadcrumb, and /health's Redis probe is a separate endpoint nobody watches during a login incident.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `logger.warning('[auth] lockout/revocation check degraded (Redis): %r', exc)` plus a Sentry capture_message to each of the four handlers (fail-open behaviour unchanged, observability restored). Swap the incr/expire order to a single pipeline, or use `redis_client.set(key, 1, ex=..., nx=True)` followed by incr so the TTL can never be missing.
findings.verify_evidence: Every cited line re-read and exact. auth_service.py 'except Exception:' appears at exactly 4 places -- 313 (_is_token_revoked, 'return False  # Fail-open'), 554 (check_account_locked, returns locked False), 571 (track_failed_login, returns locked False), 581 (clear_failed_logins, 'pass') -- and NONE of the four logs. _revoke_token (:294-302) does log a warning, but logout_user (:279-291) returns {'success': True, 'message': 'Logged out successfully'} on both the try and the except path. Contrast confirmed: cache_service.py:63 logger.error('Redis GET error: ...'). SECONDARY DEFECT RE-DERIVED AND IT IS THE STRONGEST PART: track_failed_login does 'count = redis_client.incr(key)' then 'if count == 1: redis_client.expire(key, LOCKOUT_WINDOW_SECONDS)' (:567-569). If expire raises (or the process dies between the two commands) the swallowing except returns locked:False and the counter key is left with NO TTL -- expire is only attempted when count==1, so it is never retried. Once the counter reaches LOCKOUT_THRESHOLD the account is locked PERMANENTLY, and check_account_locked returns 'retry_after': max(ttl, 0) = 0 because redis ttl is -1, i.e. the client is told to retry immediately, forever.

findings.title: Freemium quota is a TOCTOU: the check is awaited before the work, the increment is fire-and-forget after it
findings.claim: check_usage_allowed reads the Redis counters at request entry and record_comparison increments them in a detached task after the response, with nothing atomic in between, so N concurrent requests from one user all observe the pre-increment count and all pass.
findings.evidence: text_routes.py:157-168 `usage_check = await check_usage_allowed(user['id'], ...)` then the full `await service.compare_from_text(...)` at :176, then :236-239 `fire_and_forget(record_comparison(user_id, ...))`. usage_service.py:180-181 reads `_get_redis_count(_daily_key(user_id))` / `_get_redis_count(_monthly_key(user_id))`; usage_service.py:213-234 does the INCRs. The identical shape exists on the GET route (:332-371) and the stream route (:536-539). No check-and-increment primitive exists for user quota, unlike api_budget_service.try_consume_serper_image_credit (:687-734) which is explicitly written as an atomic INCRBY-then-check with rollback.
findings.failure_scenario: A free-tier user at 2 of 3 daily comparisons fires 6 parallel /text/compare requests (the slowapi limiter permits 10/min). All six read daily_used=2, all six pass the gate, all six run a full comparison. The user consumes 6 comparisons against a 3/day cap; at the repo's own ~$0.01-per-compare target plus ~10-15 Serper credits per cold compare that is a direct, repeatable overspend, and the counters end up at 8 so the user is then locked out of legitimate use.
findings.fix_sketch: Port the try_consume_serper_image_credit pattern to usage: an atomic `redis_client.incrby(daily_key, 1)` + limit check + `decrby` rollback on refusal, called synchronously at the gate; keep the Supabase lifetime write fire-and-forget. Refund the Redis increment on the failure paths where _surface_comparison_failure raises.
findings.verify_evidence: Re-derived end to end. text_routes.py:158 'usage_check = await check_usage_allowed(user["id"], ...)', the work at :176 'result = await service.compare_from_text(...)', and the increment at :236-239 'fire_and_forget(record_comparison(user_id, ...), label="record_comparison.text.post")' -- nothing atomic in between. usage_service.py:180-181 reads _get_redis_count(_daily_key(user_id)) / _get_redis_count(_monthly_key(user_id)) and compares at :184/:193; record_comparison (:213-234) does the INCRs afterwards. Absence claim checked independently: usage_service exposes only _daily_key / _monthly_key / _get_redis_count / _get_user_tier_info / _maybe_reset_referral_bonus / _get_active_referral_bonus / check_usage_allowed / record_comparison / get_usage_status -- there is no check-and-increment primitive, while api_budget_service.py:687 try_consume_serper_image_credit is exactly that pattern for a different counter. Bounding note that keeps this at P2 rather than P1: every parallel request DOES increment afterwards, so a burst of N overshoots the cap once by N-1 and then locks the user out -- costly and repeatable per window, not unbounded. record_comparison carries the same incr-then-expire TTL-loss shape as auth (:222-228).

findings.title: audit_service claims it 'never blocks the request' while doing a synchronous Supabase insert on the event loop
findings.claim: log_audit_event's contract says it is safe to fire-and-forget because it never blocks, but its body issues the sync supabase-py insert directly, so the detached task blocks the single event loop — and therefore every concurrent request — for the full insert RTT.
findings.evidence: audit_service.py:18-21 docstring: 'This function is designed to be called via asyncio.create_task() so it never blocks the request.' Body at :29-37: `client = get_admin_supabase_client()` then `client.table('admin_audit_log').insert({...}).execute()` with no to_thread. get_admin_supabase_client returns the sync client (database_service.py:12, supabase==2.31.0). Detaching a coroutine does not make a blocking call non-blocking — it only moves the stall to a different point in the same loop iteration.
findings.failure_scenario: A credential-stuffing burst drives login_failed + brute_force_lockout audit rows. Each is create_task'd and each blocks the loop for one Supabase insert RTT. Legitimate concurrent traffic — SSE streams mid-price-race — absorbs the whole stall, and because the price race and stream cap are wall-clock deadlines, the audit path can push unrelated comparisons past their timeout. The docstring guarantees this cannot happen, so nobody looks here.
findings.fix_sketch: `await asyncio.to_thread(lambda: client.table('admin_audit_log').insert(record).execute())`, and correct the docstring to say it must be dispatched via app.utils.async_utils.fire_and_forget.
findings.verify_evidence: Re-read audit_service.py in full (69 lines). The docstring at :18-21 says verbatim 'This function is designed to be called via asyncio.create_task() so it never blocks the request.'; the body at :28-37 is 'client = get_admin_supabase_client()' then 'client.table("admin_audit_log").insert({...}).execute()' with no to_thread anywhere in the file (grep returns zero to_thread hits). get_admin_supabase_client comes from database_service.py, whose client is the sync supabase==2.31.0 one. Detaching a coroutine does not make a blocking call non-blocking -- the stall just moves within the same loop iteration -- so the docstring's guarantee is false. OVERLAP NOTE for synthesis: this .execute() is one of the 128 counted in correctness-03, so the blocking cost is partly double-counted; the content unique to this entry is the incorrect contract in the docstring, which is what makes the site invisible to future readers.

findings.title: STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS code default (25.0) disagrees with the documented production value (30.0)
findings.claim: The module default is 25.0 while CLAUDE.md records the value as 30.0 since 2026-06-09, so the entire timeout budget silently shrinks by 5s in any environment where the Railway variable is absent — and inline comments still reason against both numbers.
findings.evidence: scs:1144 `STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS = float(os.getenv('STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS', '25.0'))`. CLAUDE.md Environment Variables: '`STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS` (30.0 since 2026-06-09 B0-C Item 3 — was 25.0; outermost `asyncio.wait_for` on streaming + non-streaming `compare_from_text` per L2.7)'. Comments inside the file argue from both values: scs:4244-4245 'KEPT at 15 (NOT raised to 18 — that would risk the 30s STREAM_HARD_CAP…)' vs scs:4671 'Stays inside STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=25' and scs:3571 'hard 25s cap'.
findings.failure_scenario: A new Railway environment, a preview deploy, the warmer cron process, or a local eval run does not set the variable. The pipeline gets 25s instead of 30s while _PRICE_RACE_TIMEOUT stays at 15s, so the Phase-2 + verdict tail loses 20% of its budget and PARTIAL/503 rates rise for reasons no measurement will attribute to configuration.
findings.fix_sketch: Change the literal default to '30.0' (matching prod) and update the two stale inline comments so future timeout arithmetic is reasoned against one number.
findings.verify_evidence: Both halves re-read. scs:1144 'STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS = float(os.getenv("STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS", "25.0"))'; CLAUDE.md:324 'STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS (30.0 since 2026-06-09 B0-C Item 3 - was 25.0; outermost asyncio.wait_for on streaming + non-streaming compare_from_text per L2.7)'. Both stale comments verified at the exact lines: scs:3571 'Bundle E Decision 8 - hard 25s cap on the data-fetch step' and scs:4671 'Stays inside STREAM_HARD_CAP_SECONDS=25', against scs:4244-4245 'KEPT at 15 (NOT raised to 18 - that would risk the 30s STREAM_HARD_CAP...)'. The file reasons from both numbers in the same module. P3 held: prod sets the env var, so the drift bites preview / local / warmer / eval environments only.

findings.title: _varhint_append_learned does an unlocked read-modify-write of a JSON file from an async coroutine
findings.claim: The variant-hint learning path opens, json.loads, mutates and json.dumps a shared on-disk file with blocking I/O inside the async consult, with no lock and no atomic rename — two concurrent resolutions can interleave and truncate or corrupt the file, and on Railway's ephemeral filesystem the write is discarded at every deploy anyway.
findings.evidence: price_service.py:8618-8634: `with open(_VARHINT_LEARNED_PATH, 'r', encoding='utf-8') as fh: loaded = json.load(fh)` then `with open(_VARHINT_LEARNED_PATH, 'w', encoding='utf-8') as fh: json.dump(doc, fh, ...)`, called at :8672 from `async def _consult_variant_llm_hint` (:8637). No lock, no tempfile+os.replace. Both open() calls block the event loop.
findings.failure_scenario: Two concurrent compares resolve different families at the same time. Writer A truncates the file with 'w' while writer B is mid-read, or B's dump (built from a pre-A snapshot) overwrites A's entry. Worst case a reader observes a truncated file and _load hits JSONDecodeError, which the caller's blanket except swallows, so the accumulated learned verdicts vanish with no signal. Gated behind ENABLE_VARIANT_LLM_HINT (default false), so this is latent rather than live.
findings.fix_sketch: Write via tempfile + os.replace under an asyncio.Lock (or drop the file entirely and keep only the 90-day Redis verdict cache at :8606-8616, which already survives the deploy the file does not), and move the I/O to asyncio.to_thread.
findings.verify_evidence: The race MECHANISM does not exist in this process model. _varhint_append_learned (price_service.py:8618-8634) is a PLAIN SYNC function -- I read the whole body and it contains no await -- so under the single-threaded asyncio loop the open / json.load / mutate / json.dump sequence runs to completion atomically with respect to every other coroutine. The described interleaving ('Writer A truncates the file with w while writer B is mid-read', 'B overwrites A's entry from a pre-A snapshot') CANNOT happen: the only caller is 'async def _consult_variant_llm_hint' (:8637, call at 8672), which is never dispatched via to_thread, and the two Railway processes (web, warmer) have separate ephemeral filesystems. What survives is a P3 residual the finding also lists: two blocking open() calls on the event loop, a non-atomic write (a crash or disk-full mid json.dump truncates the file, and the blanket 'except Exception: pass' hides it), and Railway ephemerality discarding it at every deploy. Gated behind ENABLE_VARIANT_LLM_HINT (price_service.py:8542, default 'false'), so nothing runs today.

findings.title: fire_and_forget returns a Task no caller retains, leaving the documented mid-flight GC hazard
findings.claim: fire_and_forget creates the task and returns it, but every one of the ~25 production call sites discards the return value; CPython's event loop keeps only a weak reference to running tasks, which is the condition the asyncio docs warn causes a task to disappear mid-execution.
findings.evidence: async_utils.py:54-67 `task = asyncio.create_task(coro); task.add_done_callback(_on_done); return task`, docstring at :49-53 'Returned for testability (tests can await it in fixtures); production callers can ignore the return value.' All call sites in app/api/*.py and structured_comparison_service.py (2970, 3365, 3382, 3460, 3987, 4017, 4740, 4896, 7147) discard it. No module-level set holds them.
findings.failure_scenario: A fire-and-forget audit or save_comparison task is suspended on an await whose only remaining reference chain runs through the task itself; a GC pass collects it and the write is dropped with no exception and no done-callback firing. Probabilistic rather than deterministic, but it is the precise pattern the stdlib documents against, and it lands on exactly the audit/history writes this helper exists to protect.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep a module-level `_BACKGROUND: set[asyncio.Task] = set()`; `_BACKGROUND.add(task)` and `task.add_done_callback(_BACKGROUND.discard)` alongside the existing logging callback. Three lines, no call-site changes.
findings.verify_evidence: Re-read app/utils/async_utils.py in full: :54-67 'task = asyncio.create_task(coro)' / 'task.add_done_callback(_on_done)' / 'return task', and the docstring at :49-53 does say 'production callers can ignore the return value'. Absence claim verified independently: 33 'fire_and_forget(' call sites across app/, and a grep for an assignment of its result returns ZERO -- no caller retains the Task, and the module holds no strong-reference set (a grep for _BACKGROUND / set() in the file returns nothing but the one add_done_callback line). This is the exact condition the asyncio docs warn about (the loop keeps only a weak reference to running tasks). P3 held: probabilistic, and it lands on the audit/history writes this helper exists to protect.

findings.title: Shopify PDP domain spacing serialises concurrent callers into the caller's own timeout budget and never evicts its state
findings.claim: _await_domain_slot converts the reservation returned by reserve_domain_slot into an asyncio.sleep charged to the caller, so the Nth concurrent fetch against one storefront waits N-1 seconds inside a 10s adapter cap; the backing dict is module-global and only cleared by a test helper.
findings.evidence: shopify_pdp_service.py:113 `_next_slot_at: Dict[str, float] = {}`; :232-235 `start_at = max(current, _next_slot_at.get(key, 0.0)); _next_slot_at[key] = start_at + MIN_DOMAIN_INTERVAL_S` with MIN_DOMAIN_INTERVAL_S = 1.0 (:106); :243-246 `wait = reserve_domain_slot(domain); if wait > 0: await asyncio.sleep(wait)`, called per redirect hop at :302 inside the up-to-4-hop loop at :298. The only eviction is reset_domain_spacing at :238-240, documented 'tests; a caller never needs this'. The outer bound is _ADAPTER_TIMEOUT = 10.0 (scs:208).
findings.failure_scenario: Five concurrent compares touch the same Shopify storefront. The fifth reserves a slot 4s out, and with a redirect it reserves again — so 5-8s of its 10s adapter budget is spent sleeping before the first byte, and the fetch times out having made zero requests while still counting as an attempt. Separately, _next_slot_at accumulates one entry per distinct domain for the process lifetime. Currently latent: ENABLE_SHOPIFY_PDP_JSON defaults OFF (:138-140).
findings.fix_sketch: Cap the reservation (`if wait > MAX_SPACING_WAIT: return None` — refuse rather than burn the caller's budget), and subtract the already-consumed spacing from the fetch timeout. Evict entries older than a few intervals on each reservation to bound the dict.
findings.verify_evidence: Mechanism re-derived; two evidence attributions corrected. shopify_pdp_service.py:113 '_next_slot_at: Dict[str, float] = {}', :106 MIN_DOMAIN_INTERVAL_S = 1.0, :232-235 'start_at = max(current, _next_slot_at.get(key, 0.0)); _next_slot_at[key] = start_at + MIN_DOMAIN_INTERVAL_S', :243-246 'wait = reserve_domain_slot(domain); if wait > 0: await asyncio.sleep(wait)' -- the reservation is charged to the caller's own budget, and the only eviction is reset_domain_spacing (:238-240, 'tests; a caller never needs this'). The per-hop cost is worse than stated: _await_domain_slot is called at :302 inside the up-to-4-hop loop in _fetch_once, and _fetch_feed_body (:551-571) retries a 503 with a SECOND _fetch_once, so one logical fetch can reserve up to 8 slots. CORRECTIONS: (a) the outer bound is NOT _ADAPTER_TIMEOUT (scs:208) -- the reachable caller is price_service._try_ucp_json_price (13813/13841) inside the per-URL price cascade; (b) the gating flag on the reachable path is ENABLE_UCP_JSON_PRICE (shopify_pdp_service.py:648, default 'false'), not ENABLE_SHOPIFY_PDP_JSON -- the .js entry fetch_shopify_pdp_json has no production call site at all (stated in-module at :76 and confirmed by grep: tests only). Both flags default OFF, so latent; P3 held.
